newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Cossack oil halts to avoid storm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Cossack oil halts to avoid storm.

text.p: The Cossack-Pioneer offshore oil platform was forced to cease production late on Monday to escape the path of a cyclone, a spokesman for the operator, Woodside Petroleum Ltd, said on Tuesday.
"It was disconnected about a quarter past five (0915 GMT) and is sailing on a westerly course away from the cyclone and will keep its distance until the cyclone abates," the spokesman said.
It would take several hours to reconnect the platform once the rig was returned to the mooring, the spokesman said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the cyclone, named Phil, was located about 320 km north-northwest of Karratha, 1,540 km north of Perth.
It was moving west-southwest at 18 km per hour, with winds of 130 km per hour at the centre.
The platform had been producing at a rate of around 90,000 to 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) when it was unhooked, the spokesman said.
The production rate is below maximum capacity of 115,000 bpd due to limitations placed on the rig's flaring system, the spokesman said.
"Because of the limitations on flaring and because the dehydration system is not working to full capacity due to the repairs we've made, we're still not flat out," he said.

The platform, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf, has been plagued by weather-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
